name: Datum Mesh
tagline: Finite-element analysis on the desktop: stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and frames.
for: Mechanical, structural, process and aerospace engineers, students and lecturers.
about: Its purpose: to show any engineer or student how a part or structure carries load, heat and vibration (where it is stressed, how far it moves, how hot it gets) in a free app they can trust because it proves its own answers.

Datum Mesh finds the stresses, deflections and temperatures in parts and structures by the finite-element method. You draw a frame of beams and truss bars, or the outline of a part with its holes, put on the supports and loads, and solve.

Frames and trusses give the deflected shape, the moment, shear and axial diagrams, the reactions and member utilisation. Parts are meshed into triangles and solved in plane stress, plane strain or steady heat conduction, or as 3D solids (extruded or revolved) for stress, vibration and heat (with thermal stress from the temperatures), with contours of stress, displacement, safety factor and temperature, and a probe that reads any point. Every solve ends with an equilibrium check, and Help › Verification solves benchmarks with known answers in front of you (a plate with a hole, a thick cylinder, NAFEMS LE1, conduction, patch tests), so you can see how far to trust each result.

steps.title: Draw and mesh
steps.text: Draw a frame of beams and truss bars, in the plane or in 3D on working planes, or the outline of a part with its holes, shaped with rounds, bevels, cut-outs and patterns (extruded or revolved into a 3D solid if you like), on a grid with snap and rulers.

steps.title: Load and support
steps.text: Put supports, forces, pressures, gravity and heat on nodes, members and edges, and set their values with units.

steps.title: Solve and report
steps.text: Solve, read the deflections, stresses and temperatures, and print a report with the equilibrium check.

highlights: Parts meshed automatically into quality triangles, finer where you ask, and solved in plane stress, plane strain or heat conduction
Frames for everyday structural analysis: load cases and combinations with an envelope of every member's forces, hinged member ends, and European steel section tables (IPE, HEA, HEB)
Contours of von Mises and principal stress, displacement, safety factor, temperature and heat flux; hover anywhere to read values
Sections from CAD: DXF import of outlines, arcs kept as arcs and holes found by nesting, and DXF export of a section
An equilibrium check after every solve (a heat balance for heat models): the reactions are added up against the loads
Thermal stress: temperatures solved on the same mesh, then the stress they cause; uniform temperature changes in frames and parts
Axisymmetric solids: pressure vessels, shafts and discs from their half-section, with hoop stress
Natural frequencies and mode shapes of frames and parts, moving on screen
Buckling of frames: load factors and buckled shapes, with every squeezed truss bar checked as a strut
3D frames and trusses: drawn on front, side and plan planes, repeated into bays, seen in a 3D view, with natural frequencies and buckling

3D solids: a part's section extruded or revolved (shafts, hubs, vessels), solved in 3D for stress, natural frequencies or heat conduction, coloured in a 3D view, with a cutting plane to see inside and faces picked by clicking
Sketch tools: round and bevel corners, union, subtract and intersect shapes with arcs kept true, slots, rounded rectangles, polygons, offsets and patterns of holes

Help › Verification: 134 benchmark checks with known answers solved in front of you, from beam theory, Euler columns, 3D frames and 3D solids to NAFEMS LE1 and LE10, with mesh convergence and solve times
Frames and trusses: draw members on a grid, press Solve, and see the deflected shape, moment, shear and axial diagrams and the reactions
A materials library of 54 metals and plastics from Datum Atlas, each with its source
Pin loads for lugs and clevises: the pin presses only where it pushes into the hole
A printed report: the model, mesh, materials, loads, contour pictures with scales, the largest values, reactions and the equilibrium check
SI or US units shown everywhere; files keep SI, so switching never rounds anything
Thirteen worked examples, from a portal frame, a roof truss and a braced steel frame with load cases to a steel platform, an L-bracket and a pressure vessel in 3D
Small and quick: a 3 MB installer, a window that starts light, and solve times recorded with every release
